extraction.body: Microsoft , the American technology giant, has issued a warning about the potential security risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) agents, cautioning that these tools could become insider threats within corporate networks. The concern is not simply that AI agents can make decisions autonomously, but that they can access company applications, sensitive information and digital tools at extraordinary speed. Such capabilities can make their activities difficult to monitor, control or stop when a security risk emerges. In an advisory published on October 19, 2026, Microsoft highlighted the need for businesses to exercise caution over the growing use of AI agents in connected digital environments. As organizations increasingly integrate AI into their daily operations, questions surrounding data privacy, access privileges and accountability are becoming more important. AI agents are designed to perform tasks with limited human intervention. They can generate code, review documents, interact with software applications, process expenses and automate several routine business functions. While these capabilities can improve productivity and efficiency, they also introduce new vulnerabilities. An agent with access to confidential files, financial systems or internal communication platforms could potentially misuse that access, whether through its own actions, flawed instructions or deliberate human manipulation. Microsoft is not suggesting that every AI agent is malicious. Instead, the company is urging organizations to recognize that an agent could behave unexpectedly or become compromised. One major concern is that these systems may be granted broader permissions than necessary to perform their assigned tasks. Excessive access can allow an agent to move beyond its intended responsibilities and potentially bypass established security safeguards. This challenge is particularly significant because AI agents can operate at machine speed. Unlike conventional employees, who generally perform tasks within human time limits, autonomous systems can execute multiple actions in rapid succession. Consequently, identifying suspicious activity and intervening before sensitive information is exposed or critical systems are affected can become considerably more difficult. Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella has emphasized the importance of distinguishing between the intelligence provided to AI systems and the autonomous actions they are permitted to take. This distinction is central to building safer AI environments. Giving an agent advanced reasoning capabilities does not necessarily mean it should receive unrestricted access to corporate resources or the authority to execute every action independently. One proposed approach to reducing these risks is the deployment of Guardian Agents—AI-based monitoring systems designed to supervise the activities of other agents. These guardians could identify unusual behavior, enforce access restrictions and respond to potential threats at machine speed. By continuously monitoring agent activity, they could help organizations detect and contain problems before they escalate. Ultimately, the growing adoption of AI agents requires businesses to rethink conventional cybersecurity practices. Restricting permissions, monitoring automated actions, maintaining clear accountability and introducing independent oversight will be essential. AI agents offer significant opportunities for productivity, but their deployment must be accompanied by strong security controls to ensure that automation remains beneficial rather than becoming an unexpected source of organizational risk.

sources.title: Microsoft Treats AI Agents as Insiders — and the Containment Layer Just Arrived - Forkast News
passages: Microsoft just moved the goalposts on what it means to secure an AI agent.

On October 19, the company announced an expansion of Project Perception that treats internal AI agents not as external visitors to be authenticated at the door, but as insiders who need continuous supervision and adaptive containment.
This follows a 27-day sprint in which three major vendors shipped agent security products.
The identity perimeter that began forming in late September now has a containment layer sitting on top of it.
Guardian Agents provide continuous, machine-speed supervision of every agent action, investigating risk changes and recommending or applying containment.

Dynamic Conditional Access extends Microsoft Entra so that a risk change triggers graduated responses: the system might preserve read access while blocking writes, narrow the data an agent can reach, require provable human approval for a consequential step, or isolate the runtime entirely.
The question is not whether containment matters — it does, and Microsoft is first to build it at enterprise scale.
Guardian Agents and Dynamic Agent Risk mark the first time a major vendor has built continuous containment for non-deterministic AI.
Microsoft has expanded agent discovery to 60 supported local types — up from 25 — including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and GitHub Copilot.
Entra Agent ID, which reached general availability in April 2026, has been extended with identity types for local and previously unknown agents discovered through security sensors.
The whole stack is bundled into Microsoft 365 E7 at $99 per user per month , which packages E5, Copilot, Entra Suite, and Agent 365.

Terrell Cox, Microsoft’s Corporate Vice President and Deputy CISO, offered the candid version: “As Customer Zero, we have learned that securing agents requires continuous visibility into agent activity, proactive protection of access and data, and adaptive protection that keeps pace with evolving threats.”
If agent security becomes a premium bundle feature, smaller enterprises and budget-constrained teams will be making do with less — at exactly the moment when agents are proliferating fastest.

The new framing: agents are capable tools that can be granted access to important systems, and that access creates insider risk — not because agents are malicious, but because they can make mistakes, be manipulated, or drift from their assigned task as context changes.

extraction.body: Tomorrow, First. News and intelligence for the agentic economy Guardian Agents and Dynamic Agent Risk mark the first time a major vendor has built continuous containment for non-deterministic AI. But the measurement layer still does not exist. Microsoft just moved the goalposts on what it means to secure an AI agent. On October 19, the company announced an expansion of Project Perception that treats internal AI agents not as external visitors to be authenticated at the door, but as insiders who need continuous supervision and adaptive containment. It is the first major enterprise vendor to build this layer. The original Project Perception, previewed in August , was designed to defend against external threats using red, blue, and green agent teams. The October update turns that architecture inward. The new framing: agents are capable tools that can be granted access to important systems, and that access creates insider risk — not because agents are malicious, but because they can make mistakes, be manipulated, or drift from their assigned task as context changes. The product details are specific. Guardian Agents provide continuous, machine-speed supervision of every agent action, investigating risk changes and recommending or applying containment. Dynamic Agent Risk calculates a continuously updated risk score by combining signals from identity, data, endpoints, cloud, network, runtime, and the agent’s own activity — including chain-of-thought analysis for intent drift. Dynamic Conditional Access extends Microsoft Entra so that a risk change triggers graduated responses: the system might preserve read access while blocking writes, narrow the data an agent can reach, require provable human approval for a consequential step, or isolate the runtime entirely. And Dynamic Permissions ensures agents start with zero authority and receive only task-scoped, time-bound access. Satya Nadella framed the principle plainly: “The most trustworthy agentic system will not be the one with the model we trust most. It will be the one designed that enables us to trust the model least.” Microsoft has expanded agent discovery to 60 supported local types — up from 25 — including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and GitHub Copilot. Entra Agent ID, which reached general availability in April 2026, has been extended with identity types for local and previously unknown agents discovered through security sensors. The whole stack is bundled into Microsoft 365 E7 at $99 per user per month , which packages E5, Copilot, Entra Suite, and Agent 365. This follows a 27-day sprint in which three major vendors shipped agent security products. Okta launched Agent SSO on September 22. ServiceNow introduced AI Passport on October 15. Microsoft followed on October 19. The identity perimeter that began forming in late September now has a containment layer sitting on top of it. But the measurement gap has not closed. The Okta AI Agents at Work 2026 survey found 96% of executives confident in their identity and access management for non-human identities, yet only 34% actually apply the same controls they use for human employees. The Saviynt CISO AI Risk Report 2026 found 92% of CISOs lack full visibility into AI agent identities. And the NIST AI Risk Management Framework MEASURE function — the part that would tell you whether an agent’s actions align with its intended purpose — scored 0.6 out of 5.0, rated critical. Terrell Cox, Microsoft’s Corporate Vice President and Deputy CISO, offered the candid version: “As Customer Zero, we have learned that securing agents requires continuous visibility into agent activity, proactive protection of access and data, and adaptive protection that keeps pace with evolving threats.” The question is not whether containment matters — it does, and Microsoft is first to build it at enterprise scale. The question is what containment cannot tell you. Dynamic Agent Risk can stop an agent from doing damage. It can narrow permissions in real time, require human approval, or kill the runtime. What it cannot yet tell you is whether the agent is actually doing its job correctly — whether the expense it approved was the right call, whether the code it wrote matches the spec, whether the research it produced is accurate. That is the measurement layer, and it still does not exist. The $99 per user per month price tag also raises a practical question about who gets access to this kind of containment. If agent security becomes a premium bundle feature, smaller enterprises and budget-constrained teams will be making do with less — at exactly the moment when agents are proliferating fastest. passages: New Delhi [India], October 19 (ANI): Artificial intelligence (AI) agents deployed within companies could pose significant internal security risks even without being compromised by hackers, Microsoft has warned, calling for continuous monitoring of autonomous AI systems as their use across enterprises grows.In a blog post titled "Securing the agentic insider" published on Monday, Hayete Gallot, Executive Vice President, Microsoft Security, said organisations have traditionally focused on external cyber threats while placing implicit trust in AI agents deployed within their own systems."Agents are unpredictable.

We need to understand in real time what the agents are doing and what risks those actions create, and we need to adjust their ability to act accordingly," Gallot stated.To address these risks, Microsoft highlighted its Project Perception initiative, announced in July, which uses AI-driven security systems to help organisations detect and respond to cyber threats.The company said the same technology could be used to supervise internal AI agents through so-called Guardian Agents, which monitor their actions and intervene when risks increase.Microsoft also emphasised the need for greater transparency into how AI models make decisions, arguing that security systems must understand not only what agents are doing but also why they are taking particular actions."Model transparency will not replace containment.

They have become active participants in the enterprise," Gallot said.The warning comes as companies increasingly use AI agents to automate business operations and decision-making, raising concerns about how organisations can maintain oversight of systems capable of acting independently.Microsoft argued that securing these agents requires continuous supervision across identity, permissions, data, networks, cloud infrastructure and operating environments."Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous.
The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

coreStoryFacts.text: We introduced Project Perception and the Microsoft cyber stack to help organizations defend with agents.
Today, we are extending Perception to secure the agentic insider .

Guardian Agents help security teams operate continuously, at machine speed and scale, while sensors, context, and actuators across the cyber stack help understand changing agent risk and continuously adapt protection in response.
Agents can be created through Microsoft platforms, integrated through partner platforms and software development kits (SDKs), or introduced locally without a central deployment process.
An agent should not be free to call any tool, API, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, resource, or other agent it can find.
Local and network and data controls must mediate those paths, observe the calls, and enforce enterprise policy.
Controlling the destination alone is not enough.
Security must also understand the content flowing into and out of the agent, including its sensitivity, provenance, and whether untrusted data may be influencing the agent’s behavior.
Agents are rapidly becoming part of how work gets done.
They can support a range of activities from writing code and researching products to analyzing revenue, processing expenses, and acting across the systems that run the business.
To be most useful, they often need access to company data, applications, tools, and other agents.
That access is what makes agents more capable.

Satya Nadella, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft, recently described the trust architecture this new era requires: we must separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.
We should not ask a model to be its own security authority.
The controls that determine what it can access, what actions it can take, and whether it should continue operating must sit outside the model, where the model cannot bypass or tamper with them.
The security system must be able to understand what changed and act before a person can manually investigate every signal.
This means an agent can become a policy target even when it was not originally integrated with Microsoft Security.
Sandboxes such as Microsoft Execution Container (MXC) provide policy-controlled access to resources the agent needs to complete its task.
Agents will only be adopted at scale if they can be trusted at scale.
At Microsoft, we are already operating in a world of hundreds of thousands of agents.

As Customer Zero, we have learned that securing agents requires continuous visibility into agent activity, proactive protection of access and data, and adaptive protection that keeps pace with evolving threats.
Those lessons directly inform the innovations we are delivering to help every organization adopt agents with confidence.”
— Terrell Cox, Corporate Vice President (CVP) and Deputy Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Customer Security, Microsoft
That requires a clear division of responsibility.

supportedClaims.text: We introduced Project Perception and the Microsoft cyber stack to help organizations defend with agents.
Today, we are extending Perception to secure the agentic insider .

Guardian Agents help security teams operate continuously, at machine speed and scale, while sensors, context, and actuators across the cyber stack help understand changing agent risk and continuously adapt protection in response.
Agents can be created through Microsoft platforms, integrated through partner platforms and software development kits (SDKs), or introduced locally without a central deployment process.
An agent should not be free to call any tool, API, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, resource, or other agent it can find.
Local and network and data controls must mediate those paths, observe the calls, and enforce enterprise policy.
Controlling the destination alone is not enough.
Security must also understand the content flowing into and out of the agent, including its sensitivity, provenance, and whether untrusted data may be influencing the agent’s behavior.
Agents are rapidly becoming part of how work gets done.
They can support a range of activities from writing code and researching products to analyzing revenue, processing expenses, and acting across the systems that run the business.
To be most useful, they often need access to company data, applications, tools, and other agents.
That access is what makes agents more capable.

Satya Nadella, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft, recently described the trust architecture this new era requires: we must separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.
We should not ask a model to be its own security authority.
The controls that determine what it can access, what actions it can take, and whether it should continue operating must sit outside the model, where the model cannot bypass or tamper with them.
The security system must be able to understand what changed and act before a person can manually investigate every signal.
This means an agent can become a policy target even when it was not originally integrated with Microsoft Security.
Sandboxes such as Microsoft Execution Container (MXC) provide policy-controlled access to resources the agent needs to complete its task.
Agents will only be adopted at scale if they can be trusted at scale.
At Microsoft, we are already operating in a world of hundreds of thousands of agents.

As Customer Zero, we have learned that securing agents requires continuous visibility into agent activity, proactive protection of access and data, and adaptive protection that keeps pace with evolving threats.
Those lessons directly inform the innovations we are delivering to help every organization adopt agents with confidence.”
— Terrell Cox, Corporate Vice President (CVP) and Deputy Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Customer Security, Microsoft
That requires a clear division of responsibility.
Independent controls establish identity, limit privilege, protect data, preserve evidence, and contain unsafe action.
Security continuously reassesses risk and adapts protection as the agent works.
Protect your people, data, and infrastructure with AI-powered, end-to-end security from Microsoft.
Greater model transparency gives security systems deeper evidence to detect suspicious behavior and inform Dynamic Agent Risk.
We have spent decades applying Zero Trust and least privilege to people.
Agents make those principles even more important.
Dynamic Conditional Access extends Microsoft Entra Conditional Access for agents so a change in risk can drive coordinated action across multiple enforcement points.
Securing agents must itself become agentic, while remaining inside boundaries people set.

Microsoft , the American technology giant, has issued a warning about the potential security risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) agents, cautioning that these tools could become insider threats within corporate networks.
The concern is not simply that AI agents can make decisions autonomously, but that they can access company applications, sensitive information and digital tools at extraordinary speed.
Such capabilities can make their activities difficult to monitor, control or stop when a security risk emerges.
In an advisory published on October 19, 2026, Microsoft highlighted the need for businesses to exercise caution over the growing use of AI agents in connected digital environments.
As organizations increasingly integrate AI into their daily operations, questions surrounding data privacy, access privileges and accountability are becoming more important.
Microsoft is not suggesting that every AI agent is malicious.
Instead, the company is urging organizations to recognize that an agent could behave unexpectedly or become compromised.
One major concern is that these systems may be granted broader permissions than necessary to perform their assigned tasks.
Excessive access can allow an agent to move beyond its intended responsibilities and potentially bypass established security safeguards.
Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella has emphasized the importance of distinguishing between the intelligence provided to AI systems and the autonomous actions they are permitted to take.
This distinction is central to building safer AI environments.
Giving an agent advanced reasoning capabilities does not necessarily mean it should receive unrestricted access to corporate resources or the authority to execute every action independently.

AI agents offer significant opportunities for productivity, but their deployment must be accompanied by strong security controls to ensure that automation remains beneficial rather than becoming an unexpected source of organizational risk.
Microsoft just moved the goalposts on what it means to secure an AI agent.

On October 19, the company announced an expansion of Project Perception that treats internal AI agents not as external visitors to be authenticated at the door, but as insiders who need continuous supervision and adaptive containment.
This follows a 27-day sprint in which three major vendors shipped agent security products.

This follows a 27-day sprint in which three major vendors shipped agent security products.
The identity perimeter that began forming in late September now has a containment layer sitting on top of it.
Guardian Agents provide continuous, machine-speed supervision of every agent action, investigating risk changes and recommending or applying containment.

Dynamic Conditional Access extends Microsoft Entra so that a risk change triggers graduated responses: the system might preserve read access while blocking writes, narrow the data an agent can reach, require provable human approval for a consequential step, or isolate the runtime entirely.
The question is not whether containment matters — it does, and Microsoft is first to build it at enterprise scale.

Entra Agent ID, which reached general availability in April 2026, has been extended with identity types for local and previously unknown agents discovered through security sensors.
The whole stack is bundled into Microsoft 365 E7 at $99 per user per month , which packages E5, Copilot, Entra Suite, and Agent 365.

Terrell Cox, Microsoft’s Corporate Vice President and Deputy CISO, offered the candid version: “As Customer Zero, we have learned that securing agents requires continuous visibility into agent activity, proactive protection of access and data, and adaptive protection that keeps pace with evolving threats.”
If agent security becomes a premium bundle feature, smaller enterprises and budget-constrained teams will be making do with less — at exactly the moment when agents are proliferating fastest.

The new framing: agents are capable tools that can be granted access to important systems, and that access creates insider risk — not because agents are malicious, but because they can make mistakes, be manipulated, or drift from their assigned task as context changes.

New Delhi [India], October 19 (ANI): Artificial intelligence (AI) agents deployed within companies could pose significant internal security risks even without being compromised by hackers, Microsoft has warned, calling for continuous monitoring of autonomous AI systems as their use across enterprises grows.In a blog post titled "Securing the agentic insider" published on Monday, Hayete Gallot, Executive Vice President, Microsoft Security, said organisations have traditionally focused on external cyber threats while placing implicit trust in AI agents deployed within their own systems."Agents are unpredictable.

We need to understand in real time what the agents are doing and what risks those actions create, and we need to adjust their ability to act accordingly," Gallot stated.To address these risks, Microsoft highlighted its Project Perception initiative, announced in July, which uses AI-driven security systems to help organisations detect and respond to cyber threats.The company said the same technology could be used to supervise internal AI agents through so-called Guardian Agents, which monitor their actions and intervene when risks increase.Microsoft also emphasised the need for greater transparency into how AI models make decisions, arguing that security systems must understand not only what agents are doing but also why they are taking particular actions."Model transparency will not replace containment.

They have become active participants in the enterprise," Gallot said.The warning comes as companies increasingly use AI agents to automate business operations and decision-making, raising concerns about how organisations can maintain oversight of systems capable of acting independently.Microsoft argued that securing these agents requires continuous supervision across identity, permissions, data, networks, cloud infrastructure and operating environments."Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous.
The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

sources.title: Microsoft warns that AI Agents could become Insider Threats - Cybersecurity Insiders
passages: Microsoft , the American technology giant, has issued a warning about the potential security risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) agents, cautioning that these tools could become insider threats within corporate networks.
The concern is not simply that AI agents can make decisions autonomously, but that they can access company applications, sensitive information and digital tools at extraordinary speed.
Such capabilities can make their activities difficult to monitor, control or stop when a security risk emerges.
In an advisory published on October 19, 2026, Microsoft highlighted the need for businesses to exercise caution over the growing use of AI agents in connected digital environments.
As organizations increasingly integrate AI into their daily operations, questions surrounding data privacy, access privileges and accountability are becoming more important.
Microsoft is not suggesting that every AI agent is malicious.
Instead, the company is urging organizations to recognize that an agent could behave unexpectedly or become compromised.
One major concern is that these systems may be granted broader permissions than necessary to perform their assigned tasks.
Excessive access can allow an agent to move beyond its intended responsibilities and potentially bypass established security safeguards.
Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella has emphasized the importance of distinguishing between the intelligence provided to AI systems and the autonomous actions they are permitted to take.
This distinction is central to building safer AI environments.
Giving an agent advanced reasoning capabilities does not necessarily mean it should receive unrestricted access to corporate resources or the authority to execute every action independently.

AI agents offer significant opportunities for productivity, but their deployment must be accompanied by strong security controls to ensure that automation remains beneficial rather than becoming an unexpected source of organizational risk.

While these capabilities can improve productivity and efficiency, they also introduce new vulnerabilities. This distinction is central to building safer AI environments. Giving an agent advanced reasoning capabilities does not necessarily mean it should receive unrestricted access to corporate resources or the authority to execute every action independently. One proposed approach to reducing these risks is the deployment of Guardian Agents—AI-based monitoring systems designed to supervise the activities of other agents. Restricting permissions, monitoring automated actions, maintaining clear accountability and introducing independent oversight will be essential. AI agents offer significant opportunities for productivity, but their deployment must be accompanied by strong security controls to ensure that automation remains beneficial rather than becoming an unexpected source of organizational risk.

passages: Microsoft just moved the goalposts on what it means to secure an AI agent.

This follows a 27-day sprint in which three major vendors shipped agent security products.

sources.title: AI agents can pose insider security risks even without being hacked: Microsoft - The Tribune
passages: New Delhi [India], October 19 (ANI): Artificial intelligence (AI) agents deployed within companies could pose significant internal security risks even without being compromised by hackers, Microsoft has warned, calling for continuous monitoring of autonomous AI systems as their use across enterprises grows.In a blog post titled "Securing the agentic insider" published on Monday, Hayete Gallot, Executive Vice President, Microsoft Security, said organisations have traditionally focused on external cyber threats while placing implicit trust in AI agents deployed within their own systems."Agents are unpredictable.

We need to understand in real time what the agents are doing and what risks those actions create, and we need to adjust their ability to act accordingly," Gallot stated.To address these risks, Microsoft highlighted its Project Perception initiative, announced in July, which uses AI-driven security systems to help organisations detect and respond to cyber threats.The company said the same technology could be used to supervise internal AI agents through so-called Guardian Agents, which monitor their actions and intervene when risks increase.Microsoft also emphasised the need for greater transparency into how AI models make decisions, arguing that security systems must understand not only what agents are doing but also why they are taking particular actions."Model transparency will not replace containment.

They have become active participants in the enterprise," Gallot said.The warning comes as companies increasingly use AI agents to automate business operations and decision-making, raising concerns about how organisations can maintain oversight of systems capable of acting independently.Microsoft argued that securing these agents requires continuous supervision across identity, permissions, data, networks, cloud infrastructure and operating environments."Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous.
The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

A lot of that activity is on Ethereum, so it was the natural place to go next." JPM Coin is a bank-issued digital representation of a commercial bank deposit held in JPMorgan accounts.
The mainnet expansion follows JPM Coin's launch on Base, an Ethereum layer-2 blockchain built within the crypto exchange Coinbase, late last year.
JPMorgan launched a second tokenized money market fund, JLTXX, on Ethereum in May.

In August, JPMorgan noted that more than $4 trillion in payments had been processed on Kinexys since the platform's inception, with an average of $7 billion transacted on a daily basis. [Newsletter][v2snippetminusbitcoin] Generated Image: Midjourney
Oli Harris, global head of Kinexys, announced the expansion of JPM Coin (JPMD) on LinkedIn on Monday morning.
The funds backing the token never leave the banking giant's regulated infrastructure.

You’ll find the black Apple Watch Ultra 2 with the gorgeous matching Milanese Loop at $200 off or this Amazon “excellent” refurbished unit down at $439 (that’s $360 off ).

What was arguably already the best value in current-gen Macs at full price is now seeing some solid price drops at Amazon this morning. While we aren’t see deals quite as low as we were for Black Friday last year, they are relatively close here – the most affordable model is now down at $499 , or within $20 of the Black Friday price. Amazon is now serving up its first notable discounts on Apple’s M4 Mac mini lineup of 2026 . All three of the configurations it offers were on sale for Black Friday for a little bit less ($20 less to be exact), as well as on and off in the lead up to Christmas 2025, but we are otherwise looking at some solid discounts here and the best we have tracked over the last few weeks since. On the two 16GB variants above, you’re essentially looking at some of the lowest prices we tracked across all of 2025, save for the bonus $20 in savings during Black Friday and a couple short-lived dips previous to that. The 16GB/512GB config in particular is now matching the lowest we have tracked at Amazon outside of the $670 Black Friday offer. Much of this applies to the 24GB/512GB model list above, but that one did see a few particularly notable discounts in May and early June of last year that had it down as low as $842 at Amazon for a short time. All of that said, for me the Mac mini is already well worth its price of entry before the discounts, is the most value-packed Apple purchase I have made personally in the last year or two, and I truly cannot recommend it enough for folks looking towards a relatively affordable Apple desktop experience. Over the weekend we spotted some $200 price drops landing on Apple’s black Ultra 2 wearable, and today we are featuring a notable refurb offer straight from Amazon. We have seen a few chances to land the now prev-gen flagship Apple Watch Ultra 2 in black at $250 off over the last few months in brand new condition, but “excellent – refurbished” units straight from Amazon are now $360 off the original list price. Amazon is now offering “excellent – refurbished” black Apple Watch Ultra 2 units with the matching black Ocean Band at $439 shipped . This config carried a $799 list price before being replaced by the new Ultra 3 but you can now land one at $360 less than that. This is an “excellent” condition refurb that ships with a 90-day Amazon Renewed Warranty. As we mentioned above, we are still tracking at least $200 off brand new Apple Watch Ultra 2 units at both Best Buy and Amazon right now. The black model with the matching Milanese Loop included, you’ll actually find $250 off select Natural models at Amazon right now while Best Buy is still offering $200 off all black case model configurations it offers – you’ll find the details you need on these offers right here . And just for reference, Apple Watch Ultra 3 is starting at $774 on Amazon right now. While we did see a very short-lived offer on Cyber Monday only that delivered a new all-time low on Apple’s entry-level iPad mini 7 models , deals are not often any better than $100 off the list prices. This is the same offer we had been tracking for the holidays last year and into 2026, but Amazon has slashed an additional $10 off some of the most affordable models for $110 in savings . Amazon is now offering Apple’s latest base model iPad mini (A17 Pro) starting from $389.99 shipped . Regularly $499, you’re looking at nearly $110 in savings here on the Blue and Starlight models – the other two are still at $399. Again we did see a mostly one-day offer at $150 off, but anything lower than $100 off is notable on this machine and today we are getting a little bonus savings. Much like we mentioned last go around, if you have some Amazon gift cards in the holster from the holidays, you might actually be able to land the lowest price ever on one of this miniature Apple tablets. All things considered, this is sort of a lot of iPad for $390. That is perhaps an odd way to put it being this is Apple’s tiniest model, it is the most affordable model that supports Apple Intelligence and I happen to think of it as one of the best couch browsers or travel tablet companions out there. I’d $499 is a fair list price, and $390 is a pretty sweet deal here. Just for comparison’s sake, Best Buy is still offering these machines at $100 off , or $10 more than Amazon’s best deals. sources.title: Apple’s last-gen Mac Mini with the M4 is $150 off

extraction.body: Best Buy has a great deal for the rest of the day on the M4 Mac Mini base model that has 16GB RAM and a 256GB SSD. Normally, it doesn’t make a ton of sense to buy the M4 model for its usual $799 price given that the newer, faster M6 version has been available from Amazon for $779.99 (originally $899) for the past couple of weeks. The M4 Mac Mini launched at $599 in 2024, and was an incredible value. Their design and ports are nearly identical, and with either model you’ll need to supply your own keyboard, mouse, display, webcam, etc. If you’re on the fence and can’t decide between the M4 and M6 models, I suggest checking out my colleague Antonio’s review of the M6 Mac Mini. The newer model might be well worth the extra $130 cost. Read our review of the M4 Mac Mini and the M6 Mac Mini More Verge-approved deals * Today brought a big discount to LG’s C6 OLEDs lineup, particularly its bigger models. The 55-inch model is $999.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Costco (previously $1,399.99), costing a little less than the 42- and 48-inch configurations. The 65-inch model is cheaper than before, too. Previously $1,699.99, but normally selling for $1,500 or so, you can grab the larger version for $1,399.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Costco. If you have a big room and budget, the 77-inch LG C6H that, like the 48-inch version, has a tandem OLED panel that offers more brightness and better colors, is $1,999.99, down from $2,499.99. * For $499.99, you can grab a 14-inch HP OmniBook 3 during Best Buy’s deal of the day that has a 2K OLED screen, a capable Snapdragon X ARM processor, 16GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. Its Snapdragon processor can run most x86 Windows 11 apps without much issue, and it’s just a rarity to get these kinds of specs — from the OLED screen to the RAM amount — at $500. My colleague Antonio reviewed the 16-inch version that cuts some corners in the screen department compared to this 14-inch model. * It’s time to get spooky if you haven’t already planned your run of games for Halloween. The spectacular Silent Hill 2 remake is down to $21.34 on Steam for PC via Fanatical, a third-party site I’ve shopped from numerous times. If you’re alright with spending more, Resident Evil Requiem is one of Capcom’s several great 2026 games, and it’s $20 off at Amazon on all platforms, costing $49.99.

You’ll find the black Apple Watch Ultra 2 with the gorgeous matching Milanese Loop at $200 off or this Amazon “excellent” refurbished unit down at $439 (that’s $360 off ).

Those offers join Spigen’s Alpine Loop-style band down at $20 alongside the ongoing deals on the official Milanese Loops , just be sure to scope out the M4 Mac mini offers that landed today with up to $110 in savings .
This config carried a $799 list price before being replaced by the new Ultra 3 but you can now land one at $360 less than that.

While we did see a very short-lived offer on Cyber Monday only that delivered a new all-time low on Apple’s entry-level iPad mini 7 models , deals are not often any better than $100 off the list prices.

All of that said, for me the Mac mini is already well worth its price of entry before the discounts, is the most value-packed Apple purchase I have made personally in the last year or two, and I truly cannot recommend it enough for folks looking towards a relatively affordable Apple desktop experience.
What was arguably already the best value in current-gen Macs at full price is now seeing some solid price drops at Amazon this morning.
Just for comparison’s sake, Best Buy is still offering these machines at $100 off , or $10 more than Amazon’s best deals.
Justin is a senior editor covering all things music for 9to5Mac, including our weekly Logic Pros series exploring music production on Mac and iOS devices.
Justin is an audio engineer/producer with over 10 years experience in the music industry.

extraction.body: Today’s 9to5Toys Lunch Break features the ongoing $100 price drops on Apple Watch Series 11 , but we also have some offers on Ultra as well. You’ll find the black Apple Watch Ultra 2 with the gorgeous matching Milanese Loop at $200 off or this Amazon “excellent” refurbished unit down at $439 (that’s $360 off ). Those offers join Spigen’s Alpine Loop-style band down at $20 alongside the ongoing deals on the official Milanese Loops , just be sure to scope out the M4 Mac mini offers that landed today with up to $110 in savings . The new Best Buy Winter Sale is now in full swing and you’ll find even more down below. What was arguably already the best value in current-gen Macs at full price is now seeing some solid price drops at Amazon this morning. While we aren’t see deals quite as low as we were for Black Friday last year, they are relatively close here – the most affordable model is now down at $499 , or within $20 of the Black Friday price. Amazon is now serving up its first notable discounts on Apple’s M4 Mac mini lineup of 2026 . All three of the configurations it offers were on sale for Black Friday for a little bit less ($20 less to be exact), as well as on and off in the lead up to Christmas 2025, but we are otherwise looking at some solid discounts here and the best we have tracked over the last few weeks since. On the two 16GB variants above, you’re essentially looking at some of the lowest prices we tracked across all of 2025, save for the bonus $20 in savings during Black Friday and a couple short-lived dips previous to that. The 16GB/512GB config in particular is now matching the lowest we have tracked at Amazon outside of the $670 Black Friday offer. Much of this applies to the 24GB/512GB model list above, but that one did see a few particularly notable discounts in May and early June of last year that had it down as low as $842 at Amazon for a short time. All of that said, for me the Mac mini is already well worth its price of entry before the discounts, is the most value-packed Apple purchase I have made personally in the last year or two, and I truly cannot recommend it enough for folks looking towards a relatively affordable Apple desktop experience. Over the weekend we spotted some $200 price drops landing on Apple’s black Ultra 2 wearable, and today we are featuring a notable refurb offer straight from Amazon. We have seen a few chances to land the now prev-gen flagship Apple Watch Ultra 2 in black at $250 off over the last few months in brand new condition, but “excellent – refurbished” units straight from Amazon are now $360 off the original list price. Amazon is now offering “excellent – refurbished” black Apple Watch Ultra 2 units with the matching black Ocean Band at $439 shipped . This config carried a $799 list price before being replaced by the new Ultra 3 but you can now land one at $360 less than that. This is an “excellent” condition refurb that ships with a 90-day Amazon Renewed Warranty. As we mentioned above, we are still tracking at least $200 off brand new Apple Watch Ultra 2 units at both Best Buy and Amazon right now. The black model with the matching Milanese Loop included, you’ll actually find $250 off select Natural models at Amazon right now while Best Buy is still offering $200 off all black case model configurations it offers – you’ll find the details you need on these offers right here . And just for reference, Apple Watch Ultra 3 is starting at $774 on Amazon right now. While we did see a very short-lived offer on Cyber Monday only that delivered a new all-time low on Apple’s entry-level iPad mini 7 models , deals are not often any better than $100 off the list prices. This is the same offer we had been tracking for the holidays last year and into 2026, but Amazon has slashed an additional $10 off some of the most affordable models for $110 in savings . Amazon is now offering Apple’s latest base model iPad mini (A17 Pro) starting from $389.99 shipped . Regularly $499, you’re looking at nearly $110 in savings here on the Blue and Starlight models – the other two are still at $399. Again we did see a mostly one-day offer at $150 off, but anything lower than $100 off is notable on this machine and today we are getting a little bonus savings. Much like we mentioned last go around, if you have some Amazon gift cards in the holster from the holidays, you might actually be able to land the lowest price ever on one of this miniature Apple tablets. All things considered, this is sort of a lot of iPad for $390. That is perhaps an odd way to put it being this is Apple’s tiniest model, it is the most affordable model that supports Apple Intelligence and I happen to think of it as one of the best couch browsers or travel tablet companions out there. I’d $499 is a fair list price, and $390 is a pretty sweet deal here. Just for comparison’s sake, Best Buy is still offering these machines at $100 off , or $10 more than Amazon’s best deals. sources.title: Apple’s last-gen Mac Mini with the M4 is $150 off

extraction.body: Best Buy has a great deal for the rest of the day on the M4 Mac Mini base model that has 16GB RAM and a 256GB SSD. Normally, it doesn’t make a ton of sense to buy the M4 model for its usual $799 price given that the newer, faster M6 version has been available from Amazon for $779.99 (originally $899) for the past couple of weeks. The M4 Mac Mini launched at $599 in 2024, and was an incredible value. Their design and ports are nearly identical, and with either model you’ll need to supply your own keyboard, mouse, display, webcam, etc. If you’re on the fence and can’t decide between the M4 and M6 models, I suggest checking out my colleague Antonio’s review of the M6 Mac Mini. The newer model might be well worth the extra $130 cost. Read our review of the M4 Mac Mini and the M6 Mac Mini More Verge-approved deals * Today brought a big discount to LG’s C6 OLEDs lineup, particularly its bigger models. The 55-inch model is $999.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Costco (previously $1,399.99), costing a little less than the 42- and 48-inch configurations. The 65-inch model is cheaper than before, too. Previously $1,699.99, but normally selling for $1,500 or so, you can grab the larger version for $1,399.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Costco. If you have a big room and budget, the 77-inch LG C6H that, like the 48-inch version, has a tandem OLED panel that offers more brightness and better colors, is $1,999.99, down from $2,499.99. * For $499.99, you can grab a 14-inch HP OmniBook 3 during Best Buy’s deal of the day that has a 2K OLED screen, a capable Snapdragon X ARM processor, 16GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. Its Snapdragon processor can run most x86 Windows 11 apps without much issue, and it’s just a rarity to get these kinds of specs — from the OLED screen to the RAM amount — at $500. My colleague Antonio reviewed the 16-inch version that cuts some corners in the screen department compared to this 14-inch model. * It’s time to get spooky if you haven’t already planned your run of games for Halloween. The spectacular Silent Hill 2 remake is down to $21.34 on Steam for PC via Fanatical, a third-party site I’ve shopped from numerous times. If you’re alright with spending more, Resident Evil Requiem is one of Capcom’s several great 2026 games, and it’s $20 off at Amazon on all platforms, costing $49.99.

sources.title: Tim Cook teases March 4 Apple special event: What it means
passages: Apple recently announced that it's hosting a "special experience" on March 4, and now Apple CEO Tim Cook is hyping up the event with a mysterious X post.
All eyes will be on Apple come Monday, March 2.
To find out for sure, check back next week as Mashable reports on the Apple "special experience." In the meantime, you can join the rampant speculation that's going down on social media.
For the MacBooks, rumor has it Apple will be releasing a souped-up MacBook Pro with a new M5 Pro chip, a budget MacBook with a touchscreen display, or both, or neither.
A more affordable MacBook could completely tip the balance of the budget laptop market in Apple's favor, and if I made Windows laptops, I'd be worried right now.

extraction.body: Apple recently announced that it's hosting a "special experience" on March 4, and now Apple CEO Tim Cook is hyping up the event with a mysterious X post. The post includes a short video and the message, "A big week ahead. It all starts Monday morning! #AppleLaunch" This Tweet is currently unavailable. First, Apple prognosticators like Mark Gurman at Bloomberg have predicted that Apple will make several announcements in the days leading up to March 4, and Cook has now seemingly confirmed these rumors. All eyes will be on Apple come Monday, March 2. SEE ALSO: 5 Apple products that could be unveiled on March 4 Instead of hosting a launch event at its Apple Park headquarters in Silicon Valley, the March 4 event will involve experiences in London, New York, and Shanghai.As is typical, Apple hasn't officially confirmed what products will be released at the event, but rumors point to three very specific possibilities: an iPhone 17e, a new iPad Air, and new MacBooks. For the MacBooks, rumor has it Apple will be releasing a souped-up MacBook Pro with a new M5 Pro chip, a budget MacBook with a touchscreen display, or both, or neither. A more affordable MacBook could completely tip the balance of the budget laptop market in Apple's favor, and if I made Windows laptops, I'd be worried right now. I could definitely be reading too much into a six-second social video, but Cook's X post looks to me like the back of a MacBook. The video also shows a person manipulating the Apple logo with their fingers, which, to me, screams "touchscreen." For now, Apple isn't saying much, and it's possible I'm overthinking the crumbs they've given us. To find out for sure, check back next week as Mashable reports on the Apple "special experience." In the meantime, you can join the rampant speculation that's going down on social media.

The post includes a short video and the message, "A big week ahead. It all starts Monday morning! #AppleLaunch" This Tweet is currently unavailable. All eyes will be on Apple come Monday, March 2. (NYSE American: GPUS ), an artificial intelligence (" AI ") data center company (" Hyperscale Data " or the " Company " ), today announced that, as of October 18, 2026, it held 210.0129 Bitcoin representing an aggregate value of approximately $17.2 million based on the Bitcoin closing price of $82,018 .
Additionally, the Company held approximately $38.1 million in cash and restricted cash.
Hyperscale Data currently expects the divestiture of ACG (the " Divestiture ") to occur in 2027.

In addition, ACG is actively engaged in private credit and structured finance through Ault Lending, LLC, a licensed lending subsidiary.
Hyperscale Data's headquarters are located at 11411 Southern Highlands Parkway, Suite 190, Las Vegas, NV 89141.
Reported $56 million in holdings, equal to 153% of common-stock market capitalization.

On December 23, 2024, the Company issued one million (1,000,000) shares of a newly designated Series F Exchangeable Preferred Stock (the " Series F Preferred Stock ") to all common stockholders and holders of the Series C Preferred Stock on an as-converted basis.

extraction.body: Five-year agreement will help simplify and modernize Ingenico's global technology operations LONDON , Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cognizant (Nasdaq: CTSH ) today announced that it has been chosen by Ingenico, the smart technology powering in-person commerce, as its global strategic technology partner. Under the five-year agreement, Cognizant has been tasked with embedding AI across Ingenico's infrastructure and operations, security and data to support the modernization of Ingenico's technology operations, including infrastructure, security, business and corporate applications and data systems, while providing managed services across end-user services, service desk, application support and engineering. Every day, Ingenico's smart technology powers millions of interactions worldwide, helping businesses deliver better customer experiences, build loyalty and drive growth. By combining seamless payment acceptance with powerful data and insights, Ingenico enables customers to reduce complexity and get more from every interaction, all backed by the security, reliability and trust the company is known for. To support its next phase of growth and innovation, Ingenico sought a strategic technology partner to simplify and modernize its technology operations and create a scalable foundation for future growth. Cognizant will support the consolidation and modernization of Ingenico's IT environment, helping strengthen security, improve operational efficiency and increase agility across the business. "The payments industry continues to evolve rapidly, with growing demands around security, resilience, operational efficiency and innovation," said Rohit Gupta, UK&I Managing Director at Cognizant. "We're proud to have been selected by Ingenico as a strategic partner. Together, we'll help modernize key operations, strengthen core technology foundations and support Ingenico's long-term growth ambitions." "At Ingenico, we're constantly evolving our technology and capabilities to help our customers grow, simplify complexity and deliver superior customer experiences," commented Tim Fulton, CIO at Ingenico. "As we looked for a partner to support the next phase of that journey, Cognizant stood out through its industry expertise, global scale and understanding of our business. Together, we will modernize key IT operations, strengthen the foundations that underpin the trusted solutions our customers rely on, and increase agility across the business to support future growth and innovation." About Cognizant Cognizant (NASDAQ: CTSH ) is an AI builder and technology services provider, building the bridge between AI investment and enterprise value by building full-stack AI solutions for our clients. Our deep industry, process and engineering expertise enables us to build an organization's unique context into technology systems that amplify human potential, realize tangible returns and keep global enterprises ahead in a fast-changing world. See how at www.cognizant.ai or @cognizant. About Ingenico Ingenico is the smart technology powering in-person commerce. Every day, its intelligent solutions help businesses turn millions of payment interactions into opportunities to deliver superior customer experiences, build loyalty and increase revenue. With more than four decades of innovation and expertise, over 3,000 employees worldwide, and tens of millions of devices deployed across more than 120 countries, Ingenico combines seamless acceptance with powerful data and insights. Its intelligent solutions help businesses reduce complexity, grow faster and get more from every customer interaction, backed by the reliability, security and trust for which Ingenico is known. Every day, Ingenico's smart technology powers millions of interactions worldwide, helping businesses deliver better customer experiences, build loyalty and drive growth. By combining seamless payment acceptance with powerful data and insights, Ingenico enables customers to reduce complexity and get more from every interaction, all backed by the security, reliability and trust the company is known for. To support its next phase of growth and innovation, Ingenico sought a strategic technology partner to simplify and modernize its technology operations and create a scalable foundation for future growth. Cognizant will support the consolidation and modernization of Ingenico's IT environment, helping strengthen security, improve operational efficiency and increase agility across the business. "The payments industry continues to evolve rapidly, with growing demands around security, resilience, operational efficiency and innovation," said Rohit Gupta, UK&I Managing Director at Cognizant. "We're proud to have been selected by Ingenico as a strategic partner. "At Ingenico, we're constantly evolving our technology and capabilities to help our customers grow, simplify complexity and deliver superior customer experiences," commented Tim Fulton, CIO at Ingenico. extraction.body: Memphis leaders are set to consider a contentious plan Tuesday to pause new data center developments for up to a year — two weeks after a meeting on the issue led to protests, calls to police and a fist fight at City Hall. The moratorium vote comes more than two years after some communities in Memphis got a new life courtesy of trillionaire Elon Musk, as his artificial intelligence company moved in amid a local effort to make the city a hotspot for advanced technology. But the effort ended up angering residents as the company installed dozens of gas-powered turbines, known to produce a cocktail of toxic pollutants. A surge of new data center construction to fuel the booming AI industry is escalating public resentment and fear of both the energy-sucking infrastructure and AI itself in the US, roiling communities from coast to coast and transforming localized energy debates into a high-stakes, multi-million-dollar battleground for the 2026 midterm elections. At an early October council meeting in Memphis — a city used to fighting for clean air as the home to more than a dozen polluting facilities — fierce opposition was on full display. More than 100 people filed into the chamber to hear about the moratorium, bearing witness to clashes between anti-data center protesters and council members, and between the city officials themselves. All eyes will be on City Hall as it considers the moratorium, which, if passed, would put a temporary pause on new data centers and on the expansion of existing ones, as well as develop a study committee to establish regulations. It would not shutter data centers already operating legally in Memphis, nor smaller data usages at facilities like hospitals and universities. Here’s what we know: How Memphis got here An abandoned factory in southwest Memphis got a makeover in June 2024, as the AI company owned by the world’s richest man, now called SpaceXAI, worked to turn the building into the “world’s largest supercomputer.” Dubbed “Colossus,” the data center was hailed by Musk at the time as the “most powerful AI training system in the world,” and the company’s website heralded plans for a second facility in the area to quickly follow. For some residents in the southwest Memphis suburb of Boxtown, a historic, majority Black and economically disadvantaged community that has long endured industrial pollution, the new gas-powered turbines represented yet another threat to their health. The NAACP filed a federal lawsuit against SpaceXAI in April of this year under the Clean Air Act, alleging it was operating dozens of unpermitted turbines in Southaven. The Department of Justice has since urged the court to throw out the lawsuit, saying the Grok AI chatbot was “critical” to national security. The data centers have also caused a myriad of disruptions to daily life in Memphis, including relentless noise pollution and physical vibrations from the centers as described in a noise complaint filed by residents; concerns of dangerous emissions from the turbines brought by state officials; and an offer from SpaceXAI to buy Southaven residents’ homes in exchange for not signing onto a class action lawsuit against it. But it was at an August meeting — where the moratorium passed its first reading — that Memphis City Council Member JB Smiley Jr. said he proposed the measure to temporarily halt new data center builds after learning Musk’s company was planning a data center expansion in the city from a post on social media. “Not only did the council not know about the expansion of the data center, the community residents did not know,” Smiley said at the meeting. “I was intentional about bringing this ordinance because I think the people deserve an opportunity to voice their concerns; I think the council deserves to be treated with respect by the folks who are pushing these data centers in our community.” An earlier council meeting on data centers devolved into chaos Members of the Memphis City Council voted on whether to delay making a decision on the moratorium for two weeks at an October 6 meeting. When the effort to delay passed 7-5, the chamber erupted. “Officers, we need to clear it out,” council Chairwoman Jana Swearengen-Washington said from the podium as observers began shouting. As people rose from their seats in the chamber and a woman shouted chants into a megaphone speaker, the chairwoman repeatedly slammed her gavel, saying, “Get that f**king bullhorn!” A livestream of the meeting showed dozens of protesters gathering at the front of the room, fists in the air as they chanted above the council members’ shouts to stop, yelling, “Ain’t no power like the power of the people ‘cause the power of the people fight back!” before the livestream went dark. Councilwoman Yolanda Cooper-Sutton clashed with members of the crowd, according to CNN affiliate WMC, as she told one attendee, “You pipe down baby, I clap back.” She also lashed out at Smiley, who voted against postponing the vote on his moratorium, shouting that he “confuse(s) the people over and over,” as she was ushered out of the room by staffers. In the lobby of the building, a fist fight broke out between two women, WMC reported. Memphis police were called to the disturbance at City Hall, but according to WMC, a department spokesperson said no one was harmed or detained. Days after the chaotic meeting, Memphis Mayor Paul Young issued an executive order to establish a 90-day study “to develop clear, actionable recommendations for regulating large and hyperscale data centers in Memphis.” “The study will proceed concurrently with the Memphis City Council’s ongoing consideration of data center legislation,” the mayor’s office wrote in a press release. “The executive order does not suspend, delay, restrict, or interfere with Council action.” State lawmaker, among four others, banned from Tuesday’s meeting In a First Amendment lawsuit filed last week, state Rep. Pearson, along with four other people, said they were banned from attending Tuesday’s City Council meeting after opposing AI data centers at the October 6 meeting and asked for a temporary restraining order to block the ban imposed on them. In separate letters addressed to the individuals stating that they have been banned from the upcoming October 20 and November 10 sessions — all signed by Swearengen-Washington, according to documents filed — the council cited alleged violations of its decorum policy, which prohibits speech including “gossip,” personal attacks and abusive or vulgar language. The moratorium vote comes more than two years after some communities in Memphis got a new life courtesy of trillionaire Elon Musk, as his artificial intelligence company moved in amid a local effort to make the city a hotspot for advanced technology.
But the effort ended up angering residents as the company installed dozens of gas-powered turbines, known to produce a cocktail of toxic pollutants.

A surge of new data center construction to fuel the booming AI industry is escalating public resentment and fear of both the energy-sucking infrastructure and AI itself in the US, roiling communities from coast to coast and transforming localized energy debates into a high-stakes, multi-million-dollar battleground for the 2026 midterm elections.
At an early October council meeting in Memphis — a city used to fighting for clean air as the home to more than a dozen polluting facilities — fierce opposition was on full display.

More than 100 people filed into the chamber to hear about the moratorium, bearing witness to clashes between anti-data center protesters and council members, and between the city officials themselves.

All eyes will be on City Hall as it considers the moratorium, which, if passed, would put a temporary pause on new data centers and on the expansion of existing ones, as well as develop a study committee to establish regulations.
It would not shutter data centers already operating legally in Memphis, nor smaller data usages at facilities like hospitals and universities.

Here’s what we know: How Memphis got here An abandoned factory in southwest Memphis got a makeover in June 2024, as the AI company owned by the world’s richest man, now called SpaceXAI, worked to turn the building into the “world’s largest supercomputer.” Dubbed “Colossus,” the data center was hailed by Musk at the time as the “most powerful AI training system in the world,” and the company’s website heralded plans for a second facility in the area to quickly follow.

For some residents in the southwest Memphis suburb of Boxtown, a historic, majority Black and economically disadvantaged community that has long endured industrial pollution, the new gas-powered turbines represented yet another threat to their health.
The NAACP filed a federal lawsuit against SpaceXAI in April of this year under the Clean Air Act, alleging it was operating dozens of unpermitted turbines in Southaven.
The Department of Justice has since urged the court to throw out the lawsuit, saying the Grok AI chatbot was “critical” to national security.

The data centers have also caused a myriad of disruptions to daily life in Memphis, including relentless noise pollution and physical vibrations from the centers as described in a noise complaint filed by residents; concerns of dangerous emissions from the turbines brought by state officials; and an offer from SpaceXAI to buy Southaven residents’ homes in exchange for not signing onto a class action lawsuit against it.

But it was at an August meeting — where the moratorium passed its first reading — that Memphis City Council Member JB Smiley Jr. said he proposed the measure to temporarily halt new data center builds after learning Musk’s company was planning a data center expansion in the city from a post on social media.
“Not only did the council not know about the expansion of the data center, the community residents did not know,” Smiley said at the meeting.

“I was intentional about bringing this ordinance because I think the people deserve an opportunity to voice their concerns; I think the council deserves to be treated with respect by the folks who are pushing these data centers in our community.” An earlier council meeting on data centers devolved into chaos Members of the Memphis City Council voted on whether to delay making a decision on the moratorium for two weeks at an October 6 meeting.
When the effort to delay passed 7-5, the chamber erupted.
“Officers, we need to clear it out,” council Chairwoman Jana Swearengen-Washington said from the podium as observers began shouting.

As people rose from their seats in the chamber and a woman shouted chants into a megaphone speaker, the chairwoman repeatedly slammed her gavel, saying, “Get that f**king bullhorn!” A livestream of the meeting showed dozens of protesters gathering at the front of the room, fists in the air as they chanted above the council members’ shouts to stop, yelling, “Ain’t no power like the power of the people ‘cause the power of the people fight back!” before the livestream went dark.

In the lobby of the building, a fist fight broke out between two women, WMC reported.
Memphis police were called to the disturbance at City Hall, but according to WMC, a department spokesperson said no one was harmed or detained.

“The executive order does not suspend, delay, restrict, or interfere with Council action.” State lawmaker, among four others, banned from Tuesday’s meeting In a First Amendment lawsuit filed last week, state Rep.

Pearson, along with four other people, said they were banned from attending Tuesday’s City Council meeting after opposing AI data centers at the October 6 meeting and asked for a temporary restraining order to block the ban imposed on them.

In separate letters addressed to the individuals stating that they have been banned from the upcoming October 20 and November 10 sessions — all signed by Swearengen-Washington, according to documents filed — the council cited alleged violations of its decorum policy, which prohibits speech including “gossip,” personal attacks and abusive or vulgar language.

CNN has reached out to chairwoman Swearengen-Washington and the City of Memphis.
Wade, an attorney for the city and the chairwoman, declined to comment on the lawsuit, citing pending litigation.
Tuesday’s meeting will feature enhanced security measures as a result of the chaos earlier this month, court documents show.

sources.title: Enhanced security measures set for Memphis City Council meeting - Action News 5
passages: MEMPHIS, Tenn. (WMC) - New security measures are in place ahead of Tuesday’s Memphis City Council meeting, two weeks after a council vote on a data center moratorium was delayed amid chaos in the chambers.
City Councilwoman Yolanda Cooper-Sutton has also been suspended from her committee chairwoman duties for the next 30 days as a result of her outbursts during the meeting.
City hall security supervisors met with Memphis Police Chief CJ Davis, the commanders from the Main Street precinct and Phelps Security to develop the final plan.
6 meeting, sparking outrage from activists, leading to the disruption that ended in the clearing of council chambers and an abrupt end to that meeting.
Read the full enhanced council security plan below:

The council’s Chief Administrative Officer Takeyshia Johnson wrote in an email about the security changes, “Staff members have received threats, endured concerning phone calls and expressed concern about their physical safety and emotional well-being.”
A federal judge has a copy of the security plan while deciding whether to allow citizens banned from council meetings back into the building.
The council also has a new emergency evacuation procedure directing them to exit using specific doors, and to remain sheltered in place together until security tells them otherwise.
The council attorney, Allan Wade, submitted the new security plan to the judge handling the case.

extraction.body: MEMPHIS, Tenn. (WMC) - New security measures are in place ahead of Tuesday’s Memphis City Council meeting, two weeks after a council vote on a data center moratorium was delayed amid chaos in the chambers. A federal judge has a copy of the security plan while deciding whether to allow citizens banned from council meetings back into the building. Anyone attending the meeting must check in through the front doors on Main Street at City Hall. Backpacks and purses are not allowed. Under the new rules, everyone must use a clear bag. Security will inspect committee rooms and chambers before meetings. The public speaking podium in the chamber will move behind the gates near council employees, and will now face the audience. Attendance will be limited, as determined by the fire marshal. The council also has a new emergency evacuation procedure directing them to exit using specific doors, and to remain sheltered in place together until security tells them otherwise. No bullhorns or noisemakers will be allowed inside council chambers. The changes follow the October 6 meeting which ended prematurely and in great pandemonium, with Memphis City Council Chairwoman Janna Swearengen-Washington banning six citizens from the next few meetings, including state Rep. Justin J. Pearson . City Councilwoman Yolanda Cooper-Sutton has also been suspended from her committee chairwoman duties for the next 30 days as a result of her outbursts during the meeting. Yoland Cooper Sutton new filing (1).pdf by Jacob Gallant Rep. Pearson and the others fought in federal court on Monday to have the ban lifted. The council attorney, Allan Wade, submitted the new security plan to the judge handling the case. The council’s Chief Administrative Officer Takeyshia Johnson wrote in an email about the security changes, “Staff members have received threats, endured concerning phone calls and expressed concern about their physical safety and emotional well-being.” She said the changes were made after staff surveys were conducted. City hall security supervisors met with Memphis Police Chief CJ Davis, the commanders from the Main Street precinct and Phelps Security to develop the final plan. Council members are preparing to deal with five ordinances and a resolution all pertaining to data centers, including a 12-month moratorium. A vote on the moratorium was pushed back at the Oct. 6 meeting, sparking outrage from activists, leading to the disruption that ended in the clearing of council chambers and an abrupt end to that meeting.
